# Somesh Mohapatra

> Somesh Mohapatra, PhD, MBA, is an AI, data science and product leader: Director of Analytics at Caterpillar Inc., where his teams build digital twins and agentic AI for global manufacturing. MIT PhD in machine learning for molecular design, MIT Sloan MBA (Leaders for Global Operations), IIT Roorkee gold medalist. Based in Dallas–Fort Worth, Texas.

This is his personal site. Every page is static HTML; the content also lives in plain JSON under /assets/data/. A full plain-text version of the site is at https://someshmohapatra.in/llms-full.txt.

## Pages

- [Home](https://someshmohapatra.in/): profile, career timeline, selected work, recognition and FAQ
- [Playbook](https://someshmohapatra.in/playbook/): a complete point of view on running data and AI in an enterprise, in 12 chapters
- [Research](https://someshmohapatra.in/research/): 15 peer-reviewed papers, preprints, talks and a patent application
- [Food Bank Spatial Twin](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/foodbank-spatial-twin/): Build notes, a build series in 5 parts. A working digital twin of a representative Texas food bank, built from a public news video in seven days for about $1.54 of compute. No CAD drawings, no laser scans, no site visit. Five parts, from why to the full pipeline and the paper.
- [Academic Matchmaker](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/academic-matchmaker/): Build notes, a build series in 3 parts. How I built a private, in-browser search that matches a CV against 181,568 researchers at the world's top 200 universities. Covers fitting the index into a static site, semantic matching with a small model, and why concept tags had to come next.
- [Michelin Kitchen Twin](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/michelin-kitchen-twin/): Build notes, a build series in 5 parts. A browser-based digital twin of a three-Michelin-star kitchen running a full dinner service, modeled the way a factory is. Recipes are bills of materials, covers are the build plan, and a deterministic simulation drives a photoreal 3D kitchen and an operations dashboard.
- [Writing](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/): long-form build notes and essays, plus 105 essays published on LinkedIn on models and inference, agents and software, physical AI and AI at work, most in the Lab Series, The Human Loop and Digital Iron series
- [Resume](https://someshmohapatra.in/resume/): experience, education and certifications

## Build notes

Long-form write-ups of his own builds, with code and architecture. Feed: https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/feed.xml

- [Why I built a food bank digital twin from a news video](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/foodbank-spatial-twin/why-a-food-bank-twin/): Food Bank Spatial Twin, part 1 of 5. Digital twins usually start from CAD drawings and laser scans, which most non-profits cannot pay for. I wanted to know whether a public video tour is enough to start one, and what that would cost.
- [From a news video to a 3D world model](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/foodbank-spatial-twin/video-to-world-model/): Food Bank Spatial Twin, part 2 of 5. How twenty frames of a public video tour became metric 3D captures through a world model, and how a Gaussian-splat trainer running on a plain CPU made them photoreal, with the code for each step.
- [Modeling the rest of the building in Blender, from footprints](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/foodbank-spatial-twin/blender-facility-model/): Food Bank Spatial Twin, part 3 of 5. Splat captures only read well from where the camera stood. One headless Blender script models the whole food bank from the operations data and publishes it to the browser and Omniverse in the same OpenUSD frame.
- [The cloud layer, a digital twin backend on AWS for $0.00](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/foodbank-spatial-twin/aws-architecture/): Food Bank Spatial Twin, part 4 of 5. A serverless AWS backend serves telemetry and operations data in the twin's own coordinates, a real-sensor path is designed and priced, and Omniverse runs on EC2 GPUs that terminate themselves. What worked and every pitfall.
- [The whole pipeline, what it cost, and the paper](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/foodbank-spatial-twin/pipeline-and-paper/): Food Bank Spatial Twin, part 5 of 5. The food bank twin end to end, from video to world model to Blender to AWS to Omniverse, with the full cost picture, what is real versus simulated, what failed, and the paper that documents it.
- [A private research matchmaker that runs entirely in the browser](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/academic-matchmaker/private-research-matchmaker/): Academic Matchmaker, part 1 of 3. Why I built an advisor search that matches a CV against 181,568 researchers without uploading anything, and the architecture that makes it possible on a static site with no servers.
- [Fitting 181,568 researchers into a static website](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/academic-matchmaker/storage-and-data-pipeline/): Academic Matchmaker, part 2 of 3. The data pipeline and storage behind the Academic Matchmaker. Ingesting 200 universities under a free API budget, compact search rows, 1-bit vectors that cut the index from 280 MB to under 9 MB, and a clustered index the browser loads piece by piece.
- [Semantic matching in the browser, and why it needed concept tags](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/academic-matchmaker/semantic-matching-and-tags/): Academic Matchmaker, part 3 of 3. How the Academic Matchmaker ranks 181,568 researchers on a phone. A 4-bit language model on WebGPU, coarse-to-fine vector search scored with lookup tables, the generic-word failure of pure embeddings, OpenAlex concept tags with synonyms, and a Nobel and Fields laureate test set.
- [Why I modeled a three-star kitchen like a factory](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/michelin-kitchen-twin/kitchen-as-a-factory/): Michelin Kitchen Twin, part 1 of 5. A tasting-menu kitchen is high-mix, low-volume, just-in-time production with shared machines and perishable stock. That makes it a better test of a digital twin than a toy conveyor belt. Here is the mapping and the bar I set.
- [Covers as the build plan, recipes as bills of materials](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/michelin-kitchen-twin/recipes-as-bills-of-materials/): Michelin Kitchen Twin, part 2 of 5. The data model behind the kitchen twin. 53 recipes as bills of materials and routings, 88 sourced raw materials, and a classic MRP explosion that turns covers into plates, prep batches, grams of ingredients and minutes of work per cook.
- [Simulating a dinner service, minute by minute](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/michelin-kitchen-twin/simulating-dinner-service/): Michelin Kitchen Twin, part 3 of 5. The discrete-event simulation behind the kitchen twin. A seeded event heap that replays the same night every time, tickets as work orders, OEE per appliance, a named bottleneck, and an optimizer that tests every fix across five seeds.
- [A photoreal 3D kitchen in half a megabyte, driven by the simulation](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/michelin-kitchen-twin/3d-kitchen-and-studio/): Michelin Kitchen Twin, part 4 of 5. How the kitchen twin renders a realistic kitchen, brigade and garden in the browser with no downloaded models or textures, binds every cook and plate to the simulation, scales from phones to a supersampled Pro Max mode, and exports to OpenUSD for Omniverse.
- [How five parallel AI agent threads built the kitchen twin](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/michelin-kitchen-twin/built-by-parallel-agents/): Michelin Kitchen Twin, part 5 of 5. The first version of the kitchen twin was built in a day by five Claude Code threads working in parallel, one each for product, data, simulation, 3D and Studio. What made that work was not the agents. It was one shared contract and clear ownership.
- [An open, cited history of digital twins, from andon lights to Physical AI](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/digital-twin-history/): Why I built an open dataset and interactive site tracing digital twins from 1880s time clocks and Apollo's simulators to live factory twins and AI world models, with 53 cited milestones, a walkable 3D factory in six eras, and research trends from OpenAlex.
- [Label what is real, the most underrated feature of a digital twin](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/label-what-is-real/): A digital twin mixes measured, designed, published, estimated and simulated data. Saying which is which, on every record, is what makes the real parts trustworthy. A practical pattern from three builds.
- [Write the contract first, what AI agents taught me about building fast](https://someshmohapatra.in/writing/write-the-contract-first/): When several AI coding agents build one system in parallel, the speed comes from clear ownership and a written contract between the parts, not from the agents. The same lesson that makes human teams fast, learned again across three builds.
